candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions so the fractional parts are directly subtractable.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include the common-denominator/equivalent-fraction operation. A and B bundle this with other rewriting cases, but the shared core across all three is denominator matching for unlike fractions.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A includes normalization inside Equalize fraction forms, B isolates it as its own skill, and C includes it within Regroup or normalize. The concept is clearly the same: carrying whole units out of an improper fractional part in a mixed number.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number as a whole plus a zero-valued fractional part with the needed denominator to support mixed-number subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A treats rewriting n as n + 0/d as part of regrouping/decomposition, B places it in Equalize fraction forms, and C includes it in Regroup or normalize. Despite different placements, the represented operation is the same.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Perform subtraction once forms are compatible by subtracting numerators of like fractions and/or subtracting whole-number and fractional parts separately in mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: This is a direct three-way match: all experts describe the actual subtraction after alignment, excluding preparation, borrowing, and simplification.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup during subtraction by borrowing 1 whole from the whole-number part and converting it into denominator-sized fractional units when the fractional part is insufficient.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A's Regroup for subtraction, B's Regroup and simplify, and C's Regroup or normalize all include the borrowing/decomposition step used after a negative or insufficient fractional part appears.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms and present it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C match exactly. B combines simplification with regrouping, so B S04 maps here as well for its simplification/final-expression component.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share the same major procedural concepts for fraction and mixed-number subtraction, but differ in granularity. Expert A combines common-denominator work with mixed-number normalization, Expert B combines regrouping with simplification and places whole-to-mixed rewriting under equalization, and Expert C combines normalization, whole-to-mixed rewriting, and borrowing into one broader representation-change skill. To preserve all concepts without losing any skill IDs, the alignment separates six distinct cognitive concepts and maps broader expert skills to multiple canonical concepts where needed.
